fix: Anchor the grep: use --grep with a word-boundary pattern and -E, or match the cycle's typed trailer or ship binding instead of free text. Test that cycle 4 does not match a 'cycle 42' commit. Switch the hang test to setHangClassifierForTest(t, true), and add a mutant check that fails when the branch is removed. Simplify the two helpers.

summary: Found by comment-reduction batch 25 (2026-09-26) and reported without changing code. (1) gitLogMatchesCycle runs `git log --grep=cycle N`, which matches substrings. A workspace for cycle 4 matches any commit that mentions cycle 42 or cycle 400, so the opt-in hang reclassifier can report a false 'already shipped'. (2) TestClassify_HangClassifier_NoShippedFallthrough still calls t.Setenv("EVOLVE_HANG_CLASSIFIER", "1"), a removed flag that now does nothing. The classifier stays off, and the test passes without reaching the branch it claims to cover. That is the failure docs/research/flag-parameter-conversion-standard.md step 7 warns about. (3) firstInfraMarker ends with a redundant branch. hasAssistantEvents could return scanner.Err() != nil directly. The test helpers stringRepeat and itoa duplicate the standard library.
title: cycleclassify: gitLogMatchesCycle greps `cycle N` as a substring, so cycle 4 matches a commit about cycle 42; a hang test passes vacuously
